title: Adding a length to a long `calc()` sum that does not fold takes time quadratic in its terms
impact: No reactions, no project named; agent-style batch report. Quadratic only matters with hundreds of non-folding terms (500 terms: ~0.1 s, 2000: ~1.7 s); real calc() expressions have a handful of terms, where the cost is negligible (a realistic 5-term calc x1000 transforms: ~0.1 s total). Not a practical DoS for a build tool.
code: src/values/percentage.rs: DimensionPercentage::add_recursive (Calc::Sum arms clone *a / *b at each level of the left spine)
summary: Confirmed on master and releases: `calc(min(1px, 1em) + ... + 1px)` with N terms scales ~4x per doubling. When the trailing length is added, add_recursive wraps a deep clone of the left operand in a new DimensionPercentage::Calc at each level of the left-associative sum, so total work is O(N^2). Length-first, no trailing length, and var() terms are all linear. #1245 (open) only changes Calc::add in calc.rs and doesn't touch this path.
repro: 1393-repro.mjs (time budget 500 ms at N=2000; master ~1.7 s, linear controls ~10-20 ms). Scaling on master (node binding): N=250 31 ms, 500 104 ms, 1000 448 ms, 2000 1724 ms. Controls at N=2000: no trailing length 18 ms, var() terms 11 ms, alternating em/vw + 1px 8 ms, length first fast.
evidence: Ran a scaling script on the local binding (master) and scripts/repro.mjs on local, 1.33.0, 1.32.0: main case over budget everywhere, controls within budget. Read add_recursive and PR #1245's file list/diff.

fix.approach: Make add_recursive recurse on &Calc references instead of building DimensionPercentage::Calc(Box::new(a.clone())) at each level, cloning only the branch that actually changes when a merge succeeds (or flatten the sum into a Vec of terms once). Add a test with a long sum to lib.rs. Low priority; reasonable to close instead if the maintainer considers it fringe.

openPRs.assessment: Unrelated path (Calc::add sum-term reduction in calc.rs, for #910); doesn't fix this. Its push_reduced_sum_term is itself O(n^2) over Value terms, worth keeping in mind when reviewing it.

notVerified: Didn't prototype the fix (no rebuild allowed). Didn't check whether other Calc paths (e.g. Length / Angle sums in calc.rs) have the same clone pattern.
